key_insight: More tumor-focused saliency maps do not necessarily explain a classifier’s decisions more faithfully.
clinical_relevance: For brain tumor MRI AI, better visual alignment with lesions should not be treated as evidence of more reliable explanations or clinical readiness.
method: Compared cross-entropy training with Contrastive Grad-CAM Consistency regularization.
Used a single-channel ResNet-50 for three-class brain tumor MRI classification.
Evaluated localization, classification accuracy, and perturbation-based faithfulness separately.
evidence_signal: In five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation, localization improved (PG: 27.24% to 36.02%; RMA: 11.17% to 18.01%), but faithfulness was mixed: insertion improved, deletion worsened, and IROF was unchanged.
watch_item: This imaging case study does not establish generalizability, clinical benefit, or relevance to cancer drug discovery.
paper_title: Localization Gains from Explanation Regularization Should Not Be Interpreted as Faithfulness Gains.
